vulnerability_summary: ZeptoClaw treated the unauthenticated RFC 5322 From header as sender identity for its email-channel allowlist, allowing sender spoofing to bypass access control.
causality: Claude-coauthored atomic commit f972f8617445474bd12d2b93a1e8f0e537d77b3d created EmailChannel and the entire vulnerable trust path: it parsed Message.from(), passed that header address into is_sender_allowed(), and published the same value as inbound sender identity. Squash 51bc07a02484ddfd2ec9c7f382dc43f829a9df86 carried the implementation into main. Claude-coauthored crash-isolation change 3ae2add445cdcc5e0d77a2f7bf1cb4abf043dd71 retained the trust decision. Release-line hardening bf004a20d3687a0c1a9e052ec79536e30d6de134 explicitly documents and warns that allowed_senders relies on the parsed From header and requires upstream SPF/DKIM/DMARC for authenticity, directly confirming the vulnerable boundary attributed to the AI-authored origin.

evidence.fix_binding: bf004a20 adds explicit warnings and documentation that the allowlist consumes an unverified From header and requires authenticated-mail enforcement upstream.
